assets.name: Bankers Hall
assets.description: Bankers Hall, Calgary's twin 52-storey postmodern office towers (East 1989, West 2000; Cohos Evamy, now Design Dialog), 197 m each, on a shared four-level retail podium. Both towers are modelled from the mapped staggered plan: a pink-tan stone wall with a punched window grid, a flat south face, a north end stepping down in three tiers, and the signature peaked crowns (gold on the West tower, silver on the East, ribbed metal hips) with a pedimented glass slot on the south and north faces, masts and red beacons; the podium parts (4, 5 and 3 levels) with glazed bands and a glass ridge over the galleria between the towers. Lit offices glow at night; the crowns stay dark.

assets.name: Édifice Marie-Guyart
assets.location: 675 boulevard René-Lévesque Est (1037 rue De La Chevrotière), Québec
assets.description: Complexe G (Gauthier, Guité, Roy, Fiset et Deschamps; Édouard Fiset, 1967-72): Québec City's tallest building, a brutalist 132 m tower of grey-taupe precast concrete on a 42 m by 47 m plan. Glazed ground storey set back under the upper floors; on all four faces a continuous ribbon of dark glass under a row of square windows in protruding precast frames; wide, plain, braced corner shafts that stand above the roof and 1 m proud of the windows; a glazed belvedere floor (Observatoire de la Capitale); a rooftop penthouse and a 177 m mast. assets.description: Harry Edward Prindle's 1915 Canadian Pacific station in Québec's Lower Town, a Château-style cousin of the Château Frontenac: red-brown brick with grey limestone trim under steep verdigris copper mansard roofs. assets.name: Pavillon Pierre-Lassonde (MNBAQ)
assets.description: OMA's Pierre Lassonde Pavilion of the Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec (opened 2016): three stacked glass-and-steel volumes of decreasing size that cascade down from Grande Allée toward the Plains of Abraham, each shifted toward the street so that the pale diffuser-glass top box, braced by a diagonal truss and capped by a gold lantern, cantilevers 21 m over the entrance plaza above a 12.5 m glazed Grand Hall; the clear-glazed ground floor, the translucent bands, the glazed stair hung on the south-west wall and the green terraced roofs of the lower volumes. The top box and the lit floors glow at night.

The nave roof is a dark grey-green verdigris (the outline's roof:colour, about 0.7 of the first pale sage); OSM tags the nave part itself dark brown, so a darker green could still be argued. assets.notes: Sourced: 258 ft (78.6 m) from the ground to the cross; the octagonal plan with four transept arms; the pyramidal copper roof with a lantern; the portal inscribed in a parabolic arch with the 7.3 m statue; the two covered ramps ending in edicules; the rectangular sacristy beside the choir; the mapped outline and its axis (bearing 48/228 deg, baked in; the portal faces south-west). Estimated from photographs and the outline (no other published dimension was found; about 10 %): the octagon apothem 26.5 m, eaves 19.5 m, gable apexes 29 m, the portal tower (24 m wide at the base, 10.4 m at the 36 m crown), the arch (16 m wide, 24.5 m high, set back 3.2 m), the lantern (8 m across, 58 to 64.6 m) and spire, the gallery depth and pavilion size, window and rose positions, the 8 dormers and the roof patchwork (fall-line streaks of light and dark copper; the far roof is one mid colour, the near mean). Which faces carry gables (the four diagonal ones, from the photographs) and the plain side and choir walls are read from photographs; the back of the building and the sacristy are inferred from the outline. The mapped outline draws the left gallery thinner than the right one, so the symmetric galleries and pavilions stand up to 3.8 m outside it. Not modelled: the interior, ornament and lettering, the stair railings, stone coursing on the side walls, the Petit Sanctuaire, the plaza and the visitor pavilion. Night: the stained glass and the dormer windows are self-lit (glow); the real building is floodlit. Flat-map grade y=0 is the plaza at the foot of the portal stair (the portal floor is 2.2 m above it). No Tesla hardware measurement was made.

assets.name: Pont de Québec
assets.location: Route 175, the CN railway and a walkway over the St. Lawrence · Québec (Sainte-Foy)–Lévis, Québec
assets.description: The 1917 Quebec Bridge (opened 1919 after the 1907 and 1916 collapses), still the world's longest cantilever span: 548.6 m between the main piers, 987 m long. Two dark charcoal-brown steel K-trusses 26.8 m apart: 157 m anchor arms rising from tall granite anchor piers to 104 m main posts on pin shoes, 176.8 m cantilever arms and the camel-backed 195 m suspended span, the bottom chords dipping in a V to each main pier while the floor runs level at 48 m through the trusses. Route 175 (three lanes) runs inside the east truss beside the walkway, the CN track near the centre line, under portals at least 6.5 m above the road. Short deck-truss approach spans to the clifftop abutments. Road-fitted bridge built on the mapped OSM Route 175 roadway.

assets.notes: Published: total length, main span, anchor and cantilever arms, suspended span, 104 m height, 45.72 m clearance at high tide, ~29 m width, K-truss, three road lanes, one track, one walkway. Mapped: the Route 175 roadway (9.17 m), the track and the walkway positions, the bridge ends and the approach roads. Members are plain boxes (no lacing, gussets, eyebars or pins); railings are solid bars; the walkway is concrete, not grating; signage and the floodlighting are not modelled. Flat-map convention: the road is level between the bridge ends and ramps 258 m north (20.0 %) and 241 m south (21.5 %) to the approach roads, on concrete girders, piers and fill, the feet placed by the mapped junctions (every link meets Route 175 at grade, Boulevard Champlain's overpass crosses at grade, Route Marie-Victorin passes under a slab span with >= 4.6 m clearance); the northbound branch of Boulevard Guillaume-Couture, which joins 93 m from the south end, has its own ramp (13.6 %, 14.1 % after the merge) drawn in separate leg meshes that Full 3D world hides; the track and walkway end at the abutments. The grades are about twice the 12 % aimed for: the 48 m deck has to reach grade between clifftop junctions.

assets.name: Pont Dubuc
assets.location: Route 175 over the Saguenay · Chicoutimi–Chicoutimi-Nord (Saguenay), Québec
assets.description: The Route 175 crossing of the Saguenay at Chicoutimi, opened in October 1972 to replace the 1933 Pont de Sainte-Anne: a plain, functional steel girder bridge rather than an architectural one. A 458 m continuous dark-green steel box girder in seven spans carries a 22.8 m deck (four lanes either side of a median wall, a sidewalk behind a barrier on each side, railed parapets) on six pale twin-column concrete piers whose square columns rise from a battered wall, and a concrete end pier at the Chicoutimi end; inclined steel brackets reach from the box out to the fascia girders under the wide overhangs. Thirteen double-arm lamp posts stand on the median wall. Road-fitted bridge built on the two mapped OSM Route 175 carriageways.

assets.notes: Not an architectural bridge: an ordinary continuous steel box-girder bridge, modelled faithfully. Published: opened October 1972; 458 m; seven continuous spans on box girders (with plate-girder members); seven reinforced-concrete piers; four lanes separated by a concrete wall; 13 lamp posts with two lamps. Mapped: the two carriageways (485.5 m, straight at 20.7°), the 22.9 m bridge outline with a joint 26 m from the south end, the sidewalks, the junctions at both ends, the roads passing under the Route 175 just north of the bridge. Estimated: the span layout (53 m end spans, five 70.4 m interior spans; no pier is mapped), the box girder running south over the concrete end pier P1 (at the mapped outline joint, 26 m from the south end) to the abutment, as far as the flat-map deck can hold it, the deck 12 m above the river, the cross-section, the box (2.5 m deep, 8-9.5 m wide), the brackets and fascia girders, pier shapes, colours and lamp positions. Not modelled: the curved concrete viaduct south of the bridge over Boulevard du Saguenay and the Route 175 overpass over Route 172 north of it (the provider's roads beyond the alignment), drainage, signage, expansion joints. Flat-map convention: junctions sit at both ends of the bridge (the southbound exit 34 m beyond the south end; Route 172 passing under 2 m beyond the north end), so the ramps climb over the end spans themselves from the alignment ends; steepest grade 6.7 %; the steel box gets shallower near the ramp feet.

assets.name: Pont Laviolette
assets.location: Autoroute 55 over the St. Lawrence · Trois-Rivières–Bécancour, Québec
assets.description: The 1967 A-55 crossing of the St. Lawrence, the only bridge over the river between Montréal and Québec: 2,707 m long. A continuous turquoise steel truss carries the four-lane deck through 1,383 m; over the navigation channel its top chords sweep up into a through arch (crown 106.6 m, 335 m main span: a 269 m arch hung on rope hangers between two 33 m cantilevers) whose lower chords dip through the deck in a V to the two main piers, flanked by 167 m anchor spans and three 119 m through-truss spans each side. Long plate-girder and precast approaches on twin-column piers climb from both shores over the streets beneath. Road-fitted bridge built on the two mapped OSM A-55 carriageways.

assets.location: Autoroute 19 over the Rivière des Prairies · Montréal (Ahuntsic)–Laval, Québec
assets.description: The 1969 A-19 crossing of the Rivière des Prairies between Montréal (Ahuntsic) and Laval, one of the first cable-stayed bridges in North America and the first with its towers in the roadway median. Road-fitted bridge built on the two mapped OSM A-19 carriageways.

assets.notes: Official tourism gives 14.3° lean and 35 m bases (technical descriptions often round to 15°); height follows mapped roof 114.7 m plus 0.2 m heliport rather than rounded published 114 m. OSM maps 27 levels; the authored 26 facade levels follow published ground/equipment/24-office count. OSM floor centroids shift 26.4 m over 110.5 m; the published lean shifts 29.2 m over 114.7 m, so the two replacement rings are convex unions of OSM outlines and corrected structural sweeps, extending the inner crown projection by about 3 m. Facade module counts, diagonal layout/width, lobby doors, colours, lit-window distribution and original monoline tenant lettering are visual estimates. No faithful corporate logo, roof equipment, plaza monuments, street furniture, basements or neighbours. Far retains both leans, open gap, silver frame and rooftop marks with half the facade rows and one third of the pane columns. No hardware performance measurement or independent reviewer approval yet.

assets.notes: Original mesh follows mapped east-northeast roadway alignment. Freeway cross-section, approach span count, girder sizes, cable pitch and fork openings are photographic estimates. Cityscape climbs to a 19.812 m deck over 250 m cubic ramps: steepest 11.89%. World uses an estimated 118 m river datum; DEM and live-provider checks are separate. The freeway is not carried by the decorative pedestrian arches. Far preserves both arches, fork holes, independent pedestrian spans and freeway gaps; reduces rail posts, piers, girders and suspenders. World west approach has a measured up-to-1.10 m offset from lateral DEM slope; shared transverse-level fitting was retained without renderer edits. Independent visual review is pending.

assets.notes: Sourced overall height 81 m and main portico 70 m with sixteen 15 m columns; mapped facade bearing 343 degrees (17 degree rotation baked once and verified in top view). Site width/depth from OSM include front stairs and attached museum, separately from the nominal 135 × 130 m monument dimensions. Final estimated floors align at 42 m; central capitals 57 m, cornice 65 m, regional figures 68.1 m; propylaea columns 20 m, deep triangular pediments 63.2–67.4 m and roof 70 m. The compact quadrigas have four forward-facing horses abreast, chariot, wheels and narrowed Victory wings, with the 81 m summit preserved. Estimated terrace levels, sculptural anatomy, Corinthian ornament, gilded mural and rear museum elevations/windows; source is original low-poly geometry, no inscriptions, interior, roads, church or hill. Front visibility, physical pediment profile and four horse-head gaps have geometry regression tests; app placement and independent release review remain separate.
